question: Why does a request made face to face succeed so much more often than the same request sent by email?
answer: Because askers forget how hard it is to refuse a face. Roghanizad and Bohns had participants ask strangers to fill in a survey, in person or by email. Askers expected both to work about equally well; in person was about 34 times as successful. An email can be ignored without anyone seeing a face fall.
move: For a request that matters, ask in person, not in writing.
ask: What request have I sent by message that I could make in person this week?
source: Roghanizad and Bohns, J. Experimental Social Psychology, 2017
reference: Roghanizad and Bohns, Ask in person: You're less persuasive than you think over email, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 2017
